correctness.rationale: Stationarity of arbitrary one-variable antiderivatives in \(y\) and \(z\) gives the two conditional expectations. Nonnegativity of \(\mathbb E[x^2\mid y]\) yields the support ceiling. Stationarity of \(z^2/2\) gives \(\mathbb E[xz]=-c\mathbb E[z^2]\), while stationarity of \((x^2+z^2)/2\) gives \(c\mathbb E[z^2]=\mathbb E[x^2(y-a)]\). Eliminating \(z^2\) produces \(\mathbb E[\dot z^2]=c\mathbb E[x^2(a+1/c-y)]\), and conditioning on \(y\) gives the factorized defect. Zero defect forces \(\dot z=0\) on invariant support and then exactly the equilibrium set. Weighting by \(x^2\) yields the stated mean interval, with the lower inequality strict because noncentral invariant support has positive \(z^2\). If \(a+1/c<1/b\) and a non-equilibrium measure never went below \(a+1/c\), the factorized defect would be nonpositive, contradicting its strict positivity.

value.rationale: The finance system is a widely studied nonlinear model, but its literature is dominated by bifurcation, chaos and integrability. The audited theorem gives exact support and mean-square restrictions on every compact recurrent statistical state, identifies precisely when adjustment energy vanishes, and forces non-equilibrium recurrence below a natural equilibrium investment level. These are substantive constraints on the model's recurrent economics rather than a transient normalization check.

final_claim: For the positive-parameter Huang--Li finance system \(\dot x=z+x(y-a)\), \(\dot y=1-by-x^2\), \(\dot z=-x-cz\), every compactly supported invariant probability measure satisfies \(\mathbb E[x^2\mid y]=1-by\), \(\mathbb E[x\mid z]=-cz\), the support ceiling \(y\le1/b\), and the exact price-adjustment defect \(\mathbb E[\dot z^2]=bc\mathbb E[(1/b-y)(a+1/c-y)]\); the defect vanishes exactly on equilibrium-supported measures, and when the two nonzero equilibria exist every non-equilibrium compact invariant measure gives positive mass below their investment level \(a+1/c\).
limitations: Claims concern compactly supported invariant probability measures, not arbitrary transients.
The theorem does not prove existence or uniqueness of a chaotic invariant measure.
The complete Gao--Ma 2009 article was not securely available for full-text comparison; this remains a literature-access residual risk.
